rows.description: A teacher sees a silent pupil who does not raise a hand yet writes thoughtful answers. Silence is not disinterest, and offering written or one-to-one routes lets that child show what they know.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A teenager feels most alive at gatherings, says yes to every plan and feels flat when left alone. The need for company is real, and it can slide into peer-pleasing or risk if unchecked.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A teenager retreats to their room after school, thinks before speaking and finds group presentations tiring. Mistaken for aloof, they usually have deep thoughts and loyal friendships.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A wise friend group plans some loud outings and some quiet ones, and does not push a tired friend to perform. Asking how much company someone wants prevents both loneliness and burnout.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: admiration, tiredness, loneliness

rows.description: A young adult performs well in interviews and events but needs hours alone afterward. Learns to choose a few meaningful conversations and to say no to the rest without guilt.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A young professional thinks carefully and shares in writing more than in loud meetings. Ideas get overlooked unless they set up small openings to speak, and managers who ask for input later see the value.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A toddler hands over a toy, comforts a crying peer with a pat and follows simple requests happily. Warmth is natural, though it can hide unspoken wants that adults should ask about.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A child says exactly what they think, argues for fairness and does not easily give way. Low agreeableness at this age often means honesty and determination, and needs guiding toward kindness in tone.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A child agrees to games they dislike and takes blame to avoid conflict. Feels safe when everyone is happy, and needs help learning that saying no does not break friendship.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: joy, calm, trust

rows.description: A teenager says the hard thing, competes openly and does not need everyone's approval. Bluntness can hurt, but the same trait resists peer pressure and speaks up against unfairness.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26
